newsitem.title: SINGAPORE: Singapore shares close higher, watch for Wall St.
newsitem.headline: Singapore shares close higher, watch for Wall St.

text.p: Singapore shares ended higher on Wednesday, edging back from two-year lows on selective bargain-hunting by local and foreign institutions.
Dealers said eyes would be on Wall Street overnight to see if the New York stock market maintained the strength shown on Tuesday when the Dow Jones Industrial Average rose 135 points.
"If New York follows through, Singapore can firm," said one broker. "If the U.S. rally falters, it will knock confidence."
Singapore markets are closed on Friday for a public holiday.
The benchmark Straits Times Industrials Index (STII) ended at 2,040.19 points, up 7.22. Volume was 196.4 million shares.
The STII hit a 25-month intraday low of 2,027.11 on Tuesday.
Of the 30 STII component stocks, car retailer Cycle & Carriage and drinks firm Fraser & Neave were firmest, up 20 cents each at Singapore $15.20 and S$10.90 respectively.
Multi-media firm Creative led gainers again, rising 80 cents to S$18.50 after recent broker upgrades.

The busiest share was newly-listed disk drive components maker MMI Holdings which debuted at S$0.53, against its initial public offer price of S$0.52. MMI ended its first day of trading at S$0.54 with 22.14 million shares changing hands.
